trust_decision.summary: Whether a user-supplied convolution column count is allowed to be used as an integer divisor; the decision is made twice, by the filter's parameter regex at the HTTP boundary (thumbor/filters/convolution.py:22-26 compiled by thumbor/filters/__init__.py:165-186) and again inside the C extension for direct callers (_convolution.c:50-54), and the published fix closes both.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the convolution filter; this is the only module that forwards a URL-supplied column count into _convolution.apply at line 30, one frame above the integer modulo/divide at _convolution.c:51 and :69.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP imaging route /unsafe/filters:convolution(<matrix>,<columns>,<should_normalize>)/<image>, parsed into FiltersFactory.create_instances at thumbor/handlers/__init__.py:196
thumbor.ext.filters._convolution.apply(mode, buffer, width, height, kernel_tuple, columns, should_normalize) called directly as a public C extension, as the fix's own test does (fix.diff:33-43)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The C module is an internal compiled implementation detail and its only in-tree caller is the convolution filter, so validating the column count at the Python filter boundary is enough and re-checking it in C is redundant.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A zero-sum kernel is legitimate: normalize_kernel already guards its own divisor with `sum != 0.0` (line 24), and the shipped edge-detect matrix -1;-1;-1;-1;8;-1;-1;-1;-1 (sum 0, should_normalize=false) must keep working, so an over-broad 'reject sum == 0' or 'reject odd/even kernel shapes' guard next to the sink breaks a shipped test and documented behaviour.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: thumbor/ext/filters/_convolution.c:24-28 (shipped case at tests/filters/test_convolution.py:30-39, documented at docs/convolution.rst:53)

O6_input_shapes: columns given as the bare URL filter parameter "0" (plain zero string)
the same zero written with leading zeros ("00", "000"), which the old [\d]+ regex accepted
columns <= 0 passed straight to _convolution.apply as a Python int, bypassing URL parsing (also negative values)
columns larger than or inconsistent with the kernel size (no crash: the existing NULL-return shape check at _convolution.c:51 handles it, badly but without SIGFPE)

O7_producer.where: thumbor/filters/__init__.py:165-186 (compile_regex building the parameter schema declared by @filter_method at thumbor/filters/convolution.py:22-26, parsed with int at thumbor/filters/__init__.py:131)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second in-tree caller of _convolution.apply that supplies its own column count (matrix_size, then a hardcoded 1).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: blur already builds a 1-D kernel and calls the same primitive twice; a maintainer adding a matrix/kernel form of blur (or a user-settable kernel width) would naturally pass a computed column count without a nonzero guard, and the published fix would not cover it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A zero-allowing PositiveNumber radius fed into _round_corner.apply, which divides by that radius (thumbor/ext/filters/_round_corner.c:46,120,186,191).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same 'numeric filter parameter used as a divisor' mechanism one C filter over; the project already writes in-body numeric guards of this kind (thumbor/filters/proportion.py:16-17), so a maintainer hardening C-extension filter inputs would plausibly guard here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The neighbouring kernel-shape branch still returns NULL without setting a Python exception (the `// TODO: error, not a valid kernel` path).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding the ValueError for columns would plausibly convert this adjacent branch to a TypeError in the same hunk, turning a SystemError into a clean error; the TODO comment invites exactly that edit.

O9_family: divide-by-zero (CWE-369) on an unvalidated numeric filter parameter (CWE-20) inside a native extension

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools via pyproject.toml; setup.py builds thumbor/ext/filters/_*.c as Extension modules with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, so a C compiler is required; tests use pytest + pytest-asyncio + preggy + pyssim (coverage, redis/remotecv as optional extras)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/filters/test_convolution.py (SSIM of filtered image against local PNG fixtures) and tests/filters/test_base_filter.py (parameter-type table, which already asserts "0" is valid for PositiveNumber and invalid for PositiveNonZeroNumber at lines 40-55)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the C divide because the report says 'C extension' (if (columns_count <= 0) { PyErr_SetString(...); return NULL; }), leaving the convolution filter's PositiveNumber regex accepting 0 at the HTTP boundary.
